name: Vegas Dave (Dave Oancea)

title: Vegas Dave Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Vegas Dave review, checked 7 Nov 2026: his old site is parked, prices last reported in 2024, no verified record, and his court history in the news.
dek: David Oancea, known as Vegas Dave, sells picks to his 9 million Instagram followers by email, not from a public price page. His old site is parked for sale, his last reported prices date from 2024, he has a 2019 federal misdemeanor plea, and in 2026 a Las Vegas judge said he would issue an arrest warrant in a $30.2 million civil case.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record of Vegas Dave's paid picks. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

short_answer: Vegas Dave is a real person running a registered business. The Better Business Bureau lists Vegas Dave Consulting L.L.C. in Las Vegas with Dave Oancea as managing member, and his Instagram account, with about 9 million followers, still invites people to email him to "make $$" on sports. In that narrow sense he is a real seller.

What he sells is hard to check. His old site, vegasdave.com, now redirects to a page offering the domain for sale, so there is no public price list, package terms or record to read. The only prices we found are from a Casino.org article dated 19 Dec 2024. His own claims, such as being right "90 percent of the time", come with no full log of his picks.

His legal history is on the public record. He pleaded guilty to a federal misdemeanor in 2019 after a 19 count indictment, and in 2026, after he was held in contempt in a civil case over a $30.2 million judgment, a Las Vegas judge said he would issue an arrest warrant when he did not appear to surrender. None of that proves anything about his picks, but a buyer should know it before sending money, especially in crypto.
pricing_intro: We could not find a price on any page of his we could open on 7 Nov 2026. His Instagram profile asks buyers to email him. The prices below are what Casino.org reported his website showed on 19 Dec 2024. They are dated and may no longer apply.
pricing: Reported site wording: next year's same package free if it does not make money
Pitched as an extra $5,000 to $10,000 a week
Crypto only, per the same article
guarantee: We could not read any guarantee ourselves, because his sales site no longer loads. Casino.org quoted his website in Dec 2024 as saying: "If we don't make money on the package, next year's same exact package is completely free." That is an extension into a later season, not a refund.

The same article said cryptocurrency was the only payment method he accepted for pick packages. Crypto payments are hard to reverse, so a buyer has little recourse if a dispute comes up. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered by any guarantee, and they are usually far larger than the package price.

claims_note: A promise of an extra $2,000 to $10,000 a week depends entirely on how much the buyer bets, and the pages we read do not say what bet size or what prices those numbers assume. No pick seller can promise weekly profit, because even a strong bettor has losing weeks and losing months.
His famous wins, such as the 2015 Kansas City Royals World Series future, are big single bets. A few huge tickets do not show that a stream of paid picks wins over time.
record: What a buyer can verify independently about his picks: nothing we could find. He does not publish a full, time stamped log of every pick with the line, the odds and the release time, and his old sales site no longer loads. Casino.org wrote in Dec 2024 that he "rarely shows evidence" of his own success rate. Everything else is his own marketing.

Court record, federal case: the U.S. Attorney's Office for Nevada announced on 14 Apr 2017 that a grand jury had indicted him on nine counts of misuse of Social Security numbers and 10 counts of causing false currency transaction reports, alleging he opened casino player accounts with numbers that were not his. He pleaded not guilty at his arraignment, the Review-Journal reported. The Review-Journal reported in Jan 2019 that he pleaded guilty to a single misdemeanor and agreed to a $550,000 civil forfeiture, and in May 2019 that U.S. District Judge Jennifer Dorsey sentenced him to three years of probation, problem gambling counseling and 150 hours of community service, and ordered him to stay out of Nevada sportsbooks for three years.

Court record, civil case: the Las Vegas Review-Journal reported on 14 Nov 2025 that District Judge Timothy Williams had ordered him in July 2025 to pay $30.2 million to Cabo Platinum, a vacation rental company that managed his villas in Mexico, and that his attorney had filed notice of an appeal. On 14 Aug 2026 the Review-Journal, republished by CDC Gaming Reports, reported that after he was held in contempt in that civil suit and ordered to turn over assets or go into custody, he did not appear before District Judge Joe Hardy to surrender, and the judge said he would issue an arrest warrant. We found no Review-Journal report, as of 7 Nov 2026, that he has been arrested.
These are court matters, not findings about his picks. They are listed because a buyer is asked to pay him directly, in crypto, with no public terms.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Vegas Dave pick service is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: he has claimed to be right 90 percent of the time. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Vegas Dave is very thin. Despite his huge following, we found almost no first hand reports from people who paid for his picks. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: The Better Business Bureau lists Vegas Dave Consulting L.L.C. as not accredited, rated A+, and says it has no complaints filed with BBB in the last 3 years. A BBB rating reflects complaint history and public data, not whether the picks win.
Trustpilot had no page for vegasdave.com, Reddit blocked our search, and we found no TheRX, Covers or SBR thread with buyers describing his paid picks. We could not count any customer reviews.
His Instagram shows a luxury lifestyle, villas and travel, and points readers to email him about picks. Posts are chosen by the seller and say nothing about what a typical buyer earns.

conflicts: We could not open his sales pages, so we could not check them for sportsbook affiliate links, promo codes or revenue share deals, and we make no claim either way.
His Instagram profile also promotes his own villa rental business in Cabo. That is a separate business, but it means his social posts are marketing for more than one product.
strengths: A registered LLC with a named managing member and a BBB profile with no complaints in the last 3 years.
He is a public figure, so there is a long trail in the press of what he has claimed and when.
The guarantee wording reported in 2024 was specific: a losing season package was to be repeated free the next season.
concerns: No public price list, terms or record. His old site is parked for sale and buyers are asked to email him.
Profit promises of thousands of dollars a week, and a 90 percent claim, with no full log behind them.
Crypto only payment, as reported in 2024, and no cash refund terms found.
A 2019 federal misdemeanor plea, and a 2026 civil contempt finding and an arrest warrant announced when he did not appear to surrender, as reported by the Review-Journal.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real person with a registered business, Vegas Dave Consulting L.L.C., and he still markets picks on Instagram. We could not verify that his picks win, and he pleaded guilty to a federal misdemeanor in 2019 and faces two 2026 arrest warrants in a civil contempt case, as reported by major news outlets.
How much does Vegas Dave cost?

We found no current price page on 7 Nov 2026; his Instagram asks buyers to email him. Casino.org reported in Dec 2024 that his site listed a $199 Daily Card, a $495 Super Goat package and an NFL season package for $995 to $1,495, payable in crypto only.
Does Vegas Dave have a verified record?
No. We found no full, time stamped log of his picks from him or any third party. His 90 percent claim and weekly profit promises are his own marketing.

For the money you get picks from a famous bettor known for big futures wins. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and with no public terms and crypto payment, a buyer has little protection if things go wrong.
